claims.claim: On September 9, HoneyBook announced a plugin that connects its client-management service to ChatGPT.
An existing HoneyBook user can connect her account, then ask ChatGPT about the projects, contracts, invoices and payments stored there.
OpenAI’s official listing says the plugin requires a HoneyBook account.
You could ask which payments are overdue, where a project stands or have a proposal prepared from a saved template.
HoneyBook says anything the plugin builds stays a draft. Nothing sends, changes or reaches a client until you review and approve it.
When connecting, you choose which HoneyBook resources it can reach, and you can disconnect it later in ChatGPT settings without changing your HoneyBook account.

HoneyBook is now in ChatGPT: whatever your business needs, just ask
September 9, 2026
Yesterday, HoneyBook was picked by OpenAI as one of sixteen tools in the new Small Business collection inside ChatGPT.
Now when you connect your HoneyBook account, ChatGPT can answer questions about your actual business, not generic advice.
Everything the AI builds lands as a draft. Nothing sends, changes, or goes out until you've reviewed and approved it.
When you connect, you choose exactly which parts of HoneyBook ChatGPT can reach. Nothing is handed over by default. And if you ever want to disconnect, you can do it anytime from your ChatGPT settings without touching your HoneyBook account.

When you connect, you choose exactly which parts of HoneyBook ChatGPT can reach. Nothing is handed over by default. And if you ever want to disconnect, you can do it anytime from your ChatGPT settings without touching your HoneyBook account.

HoneyBook helps independent businesses handle inquiries, proposals, contracts, invoices, and payments in one place. Connect your HoneyBook account to ChatGPT and work through a job without jumping between tabs. Ask which leads need a follow-up, create a proposal from your own template, review it before it goes anywhere, and then ask who still owes you money and raise a payment request.
You approve what it can reach before anything runs, resource by resource, and nothing reaches a client until you send it. Requests are isolated, and credentials are not shared with the model.
Requires a HoneyBook account.
